attributes.residual: PROPOSED FIXES, in payoff order and all cheap. (a) hv_formfirst: catch nothing -- fix the call, or fail LOUD. A sweep that turns an exception into a per-candidate 'refuses' line and then totals those lines is the one output shape that cannot be distinguished from a real negative, and this project's rule is that an absence claim quotes its command AND its output; here the command's output IS the fabricated absence. The minimum acceptable behaviour is a non-zero exit with 'N candidates ABORTED, not refused' kept separate from the CLOSE count. (b) wr_try_rule: fill the window hashes the same way it fills the function's -- it already has both objects open and the permutation is deterministic -- or raise the named error pointing at wr_perm_hash.py. (c) rule_derive.py and build_rule.py: either take a unit/function argument or move under composed_census with a lane prefix; a general name in tools/gdl is a promise the file does not keep, and it cost this lane two invocations to discover. SCREEN FOR WHAT ELSE HAS THIS SHAPE, per AGENTS.md discipline 18: the crash-as-refusal pattern has now been recorded twice at two layers (webfrank's own check_permutation_dependences in run 31, hv_formfirst's classifier call here), and the sibling call sites to check are the other hv_* sweeps promoted in the same commit -- hv_perm.py, hv_repair.py, hv_sweep.py, hv_rctrace.py, hv_bypass.py, hv_try.py -- all of which classify candidates in a loop and print per-candidate verdicts. hv_try.py additionally crashes with an IndexError on --help (it reads sys.argv positionally with no argparse), so at least two of the seven do not survive the cheapest possible invocation.

attributes.verification: Each finding is one command with its verbatim output. (1) `python tools/gdl/composed_census/hv_formfirst.py --help` -- the tool ignores --help, runs its sweep, and prints eight lines of the form 'refuses game/enemy/critter::CritterLoadDone -- TypeError: corrected_classify() got an unexpected keyword argument \'form_first\'' followed by '0 of 8 CLOSE under the corrected arrow order', then exits 1. Every one of the eight refusals IS the same TypeError, so the summary line is a manufactured negative: the tool never classified anything. It also CONTRADICTS its own founding record without saying so -- claim.HV_regfield-only-class-full-image-sweep-and-its-exhaustion.20260901.v1 records that under the corrected arrow order one of exactly these eight CLOSES ('fn_80054E78, withheld for provenance'), so the live tool now disagrees with the accepted record and the disagreement is invisible in its output. A lane quoting '0 of 8' as a screen would park a function the corpus already measured closable. (2) `python tools/gdl/composed_census/wr_try_rule.py <unit> <fn> <fragment>` with an instruction_permutation window crashes with a bare 'KeyError: before_sha256' from webfrank.py line 4058: the tool fills the FUNCTION's before/after hashes from the live objects but not the per-WINDOW ones, and webfrank's own code raises a NAMED authoring error for the analogous missing 'at' key ('copy-form edit missing its at key ... each equivalent_copy_form edit needs at (byte offset)') precisely because a bare traceback was once misread as a tool bug. The window hashes come from `wr_perm_hash.py`, which is a separate tool nothing points to from wr_try_rule's docstring or error. (3) `python tools/gdl/rule_derive.py --help` and `python tools/gdl/composed_census/wf_mkrule.py --help`: rule_derive ignores --help and dumps a hardcoded pb_window analysis (pbWinSetup, pbProjCalc) -- it is a single-TU script under a fully general name in the CORE tools directory, next to fndiff and probe. `build_rule.py --help` does the same. wf_mkrule at least parses --help but AGENTS.md discipline 17(a) already records it writing a generic 'rule.json'.
